evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that selection state and sorting capabilities persist after browsing/searching completes, supporting downstream actions without re-initiating the use case.

evidence_cards.content: After the User successfully browses files and archives, the system state is characterized by the display of a list of available drives (e.g., 'Vista (C:)', 'My Passport (D:)') with columns for Name, Type, Size (B), Free space, and Filesystem.

source_locations.location: Top screenshot showing the PeaZip interface with drive list

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state upon successful completion of the browsing action (Main Flow Step 3).

evidence_cards.content: The bottom status bar of the PeaZip interface displays the current browsing context path (e.g., 'Browsing: USER-PC [user]'), confirming the location within the hierarchy after navigation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides specific feedback to the user regarding their current position in the file system after browsing.

evidence_cards.content: After successful browsing or searching, the system state allows the User to preview selected objects with associated applications via double-click, activate context menus via right-click, or extract selected objects via middle button click.

source_locations.location: Page 30, under 'File manager's mouse controls' section

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These mouse control behaviors define the immediate post-browse/search system state where objects are selectable and actionable for preview or extraction.

evidence_cards.content: Upon completion of a search (recursive or non-recursive), the system displays results within the current folder or subfolders as specified by the search mode triggered (F3 or Ctrl+F3).

source_locations.location: Page 29, under 'Navigation' section listing F3 and Ctrl+F3 functions

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable outcome state after executing a search command — results are displayed in scope defined by the search type.

evidence_cards.content: After successful browsing or searching, the system displays a list of files and archives in the PeaZip file manager interface, showing columns for Name, Type, Size (B), Packed Date/time, Attributes, and CRC.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the observable system state immediately after the use case completes successfully: the user sees a structured list of browsed/searched objects with metadata.

evidence_cards.content: The PeaZip file manager interface is the display container for browse and search results, as shown in Figure 2 titled 'Basic application interface(file manager interface)'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that the postcondition state — displaying results — occurs within the specific UI component identified as the file manager interface, resolving ambiguity about where results appear.

evidence_cards.content: After successful browsing or searching, the system displays results in the PeaZip file manager interface, showing object details such as Name, Type, Size (B), Free space, and Filesystem for drives, or Name, Type, Size (B), Folders, Files, Date/time, Attributes, and Full name for archived contents.

source_locations.location: First screenshot (USER-PC window) and second screenshot ('Create .zip, new archive' window under 'Archiving:' section)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable post-use-case state: structured display of browsed/searched objects with metadata columns, confirming completion of browse/search interaction.

evidence_cards.content: The status bar at the bottom of the PeaZip interface updates to reflect the current browsing context (e.g., 'Browsing: USER-PC [user]' or '0 dir(s), 0 file(s), 0 B'), indicating successful navigation or search result set size.

source_locations.location: Status bar in both screenshots — first shows 'Browsing: USER-PC [user]', second shows '0 dir(s), 0 file(s), 0 B'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides immediate user feedback upon completion of browse/search, serving as a measurable postcondition indicator of system state.

evidence_cards.content: The File Manager Interface is connected to the 'Graphic display of currently executed functions' component.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that after successful browsing or searching (executed functions), the system provides a graphic display as part of the resulting state.

evidence_cards.content: The User interacts directly with the Extract Interface and Create Archive Interface components in addition to the File Manager Interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the scope of the post-browse state where the user may transition to other interfaces, implying the browse/search session has concluded or paused.
